chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Nadr ibn Qirwash, who said:

Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him) said: 'As-Sawiq, when you wash it seven times and transfer it from one vessel to another, it removes fever and brings strength to the two legs and the two feet.'

key_terms.السَّوِيقُ: A traditional food made from flour, often wheat, cooked with water or milk; here referred to as a medicinal remedy.

ai.seo_question: What are the medicinal benefits of washing and transferring As-Sawiq according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Madi (peace be upon him) prescribes a specific physical preparation for As-Sawiq—washing it seven times and transferring it between vessels—to treat fever and strengthen the lower limbs. This practice reflects the Shia tradition of combining spiritual intention with practical, empirical medicine, where the ritualistic washing enhances the therapeutic efficacy of the wheat-based porridge.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Nazar Bin Qirwash who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) said: ‘When Al-Suweyq is washed even times, and transferred from a vessel to another vessel, so it does away with the fever and the strength comes to the two legs and the two feet’.
en.sarwar: 9. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Nadr ibn Qarwash who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan, al-Awwal, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If you turn sawiq seven times upside down and change its place from one pot into the other it then can remove fever and send power to the legs and feet.’”
